name: Zhēng Fēn
description: Zhēng Fēn ('Competing for Points') is a Chinese climbing/point-trick hybrid. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Shed cards through ascending combinations. Point cards: 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts. 100 total per hand. First out gets LAST player's tricks + remaining cards. Last out scores 0. Play to 500/1000.

history.origins: Zhēng Fēn (挣分, 'competing for points') is a traditional Chinese card game, a hybrid of climbing and point-trick (king-ten-five group). Documented in the West in 1985 by Axel Schmale in Pöppel-Revue after he learned it in China during a railway journey; it shares mechanics with Zheng Shangyou and Big Two and point values with Da Bai Fen (Hundred).
timeline: 1985: Documented in Pöppel-Revue by Axel Schmale; learned in China during a railway journey.

setup.deck: 54 cards (52 + two distinguishable jokers, big and small).
setup.dealing: Anticlockwise. First deal: a randomly chosen player shuffles, right-hand neighbour cuts. Players take one card at a time from the face-down pack, anticlockwise, until all cards are distributed; some may have one more card than others.

rules.objective: Win valuable cards in tricks (5s = 5 pts, 10s and Ks = 10 pts; 100 points per hand). First player to reach the agreed target (usually 500 or 1000) wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Climbing: play higher combinations (singles/pairs/triples/sequences). 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts. 100 total. First out = get last player's tricks. Last out = 0 points. Accumulate score over rounds.
keyRules: First out wins last player's tricks

strategy.basic: Shed fast to avoid being last.

scoring.description: 5=5pts, 10=10pts, K=10pts. Last player = 0pts. First player gets their tricks. Target 500/1000.
